tasks.gr9-sharpeville-1960-t4: Topic: Sharpeville 1960. Cover the March 21, 1960 Sharpeville Massacre where police killed 69 unarmed protesters and wounded 180 during a PAC-organized pass law protest, the declaration of a state of emergency by the government, the banning of the ANC and PAC, international condemnation and beginning of economic sanctions, and the formation of Umkhonto we Sizwe (MK)—the ANC's armed wing led by Nelson Mandela—in December 1961 as a response to state violence and legal suppression. Ask Grade 9 learners to explain why Sharpeville was a turning point, analyze how state violence shaped resistance strategy, evaluate international response to the massacre, describe the shift from non-violence to armed struggle, and analyze the moral dilemmas faced by resistance movements under brutal oppression.
tasks.gr9-soweto-uprising-1976-t4: Topic: Soweto Uprising 1976. Cover the June 16, 1976 youth-led uprising in Soweto protesting the Bantu Education Act and forced use of Afrikaans, police violence and hundreds of deaths, students burning government buildings and clashing with police, nationwide spread of uprisings, boycotts, and stay-aways, the discrediting of apartheid in the eyes of millions through images of violence against children, the role of youth as central to liberation struggles, June 16 now celebrated as South Africa's Youth Day, and the uprising's acceleration of apartheid's decline. Ask Grade 9 learners to explain why youth led the uprising, analyze the choice of targets (schools, Afrikaans), describe the spread of resistance nationwide, evaluate the impact of violent response to student protests, and discuss how the uprising changed apartheid's international standing.
tasks.gr9-mandela-release-unbanning-t4: Topic: Mandela's Release and Unbanning. Cover Nelson Mandela's imprisonment for 27 years (1962–1990) on Robben Island and other prisons, his refusal to renounce the struggle despite brutal conditions, Mandela's transformation into a global icon with 'Free Mandela' campaigns, President F. W. de Klerk's announcement on February 2, 1990 of the unbanning of the ANC and other organizations, Mandela's release on February 11, 1990 at age 71, his message of reconciliation rather than revenge, and his leadership in uniting the anti-apartheid movement and beginning negotiations with the government. Ask Grade 9 learners to evaluate Mandela's role in resistance, analyze the significance of unbanning, explain why Mandela's release was global news, evaluate his message of reconciliation, and discuss how his leadership shaped the transition to democracy.
tasks.gr9-negotiations-1994-election-t4: Topic: Negotiations and 1994 Election. Cover multi-party negotiations (1990–1994) between the government, ANC, and other organizations, the drafting of a new Constitution and Bill of Rights guaranteeing equality and democracy, the historic first democratic election on April 27, 1994 with universal adult suffrage where all races could vote, Nelson Mandela's election as president, the declaration of April 27 as Freedom Day, the establishment of the Truth and Reconciliation Commission to address past abuses through truth-telling rather than revenge alone, and South Africa's transition from apartheid to democracy as a model for post-conflict societies. Ask Grade 9 learners to analyze multi-party negotiations, explain the new Constitution's guarantee of rights, evaluate universal suffrage as a breakthrough, assess the Truth and Reconciliation Commission approach to justice, and discuss South Africa's post-apartheid transition as a historical turning point.
